name: Protein-sparing modified fast

card.summary: A very-low-calorie, protein-centred diet used for rapid fat loss while aiming to keep muscle, giving a leaner, more defined look.
card.note: Clinical versions are medically supervised; unsupervised very-low-calorie diets are linked to muscle loss, gallstones and electrolyte problems.

quick.overview:
The protein-sparing modified fast (PSMF) is a very-low-calorie diet made up mostly of protein with very little carbohydrate and fat. It was developed in clinical nutrition to produce large, rapid fat loss in people with obesity while limiting the loss of lean tissue.

In physique and bodybuilding circles it is used as a short cut-phase to get lean quickly, since less body fat makes muscle definition and facial leanness more visible. Clinical reviews describe it as effective for fast weight loss under supervision, with caveats about regain and risks.
quick.how: Followers eat lean protein sources and non-starchy vegetables with supplements, usually for limited blocks of weeks and often alongside resistance training to help keep muscle. Medical programmes use calorie intakes in the range of roughly 400 to 800 per day with monitoring and a structured return to normal eating.
quick.risks: Documented concerns include loss of lean mass, gallstones, constipation, electrolyte disturbances and a lower resting metabolic rate during weight loss. Liquid protein diets in the late 1970s were linked to deaths in the US. Clinical guidance describes candidates as people with substantial weight to lose and recommends medical supervision.

lead: The protein-sparing modified fast (PSMF) is a very-low-calorie diet in which nearly all energy comes from protein, supplemented with fluids, vitamins and minerals, and with very little carbohydrate or fat. It was developed in clinical nutrition in the 1970s, notably in the research of George Blackburn, as a way to produce large, fast fat loss in people with obesity while limiting the loss of muscle protein.[3][4][5][21]

In physique and looksmaxxing circles the attraction is visible leanness in a short time. Lower body fat makes muscle definition, vascularity and facial contours more apparent, so PSMF is used as a brief, aggressive cutting phase before an event, photo or holiday, usually alongside resistance training intended to hold on to muscle.[2][18] The best-known lifter-oriented version is the one set out in Lyle McDonald's 2005 book The Rapid Fat Loss Handbook, which adapted the clinical idea for bodybuilders and strength athletes.[18]

Clinical reviews describe the supervised form as effective for losing a large amount of weight relatively quickly when combined with exercise, behaviour change and education.[6] The research base consists mostly of studies in people with obesity, including type 2 diabetes and pre-surgical patients; the same literature documents weight regain, a fall in resting metabolic rate, and the 1970s liquid protein deaths that shaped regulation of very-low-calorie products.[7][8][12][22]

chain: Calories drop sharply, almost all from lean protein
Body fat falls quickly while protein and lifting aim to retain muscle
Leaner face and visible muscle definition
angle.text: PSMF cuts body fat quickly while a high protein intake and training aim to retain muscle, so the physique and face look leaner and more defined in a matter of weeks. Lifters use it as a short cutting phase before a photo, event or the next training block.

paras: In clinical form the diet supplies protein in the range of 1.2 to 1.4 g per kg of ideal body weight with free fluids and vitamin and mineral supplements; ketone bodies rise and hunger is described as well controlled.[4][9] Wikipedia describes protein as set at the minimum judged necessary to limit muscle loss, since protein beyond that is thought to be converted into glucose and so would not add to the fasting-like state.[21]

Medically supervised versions use complete protein sources such as meat, fish, eggs, cheese or tofu, or formulated liquid protein, with daily vitamin, mineral and electrolyte supplementation and a gradual return to normal eating.[21][22] A very-low-calorie diet is conventionally defined as 800 kilocalories or fewer per day, and the PSMF is classed as a protein-centred type of VLCD.[12][21]

George Blackburn (1936-2017) trained as a biochemist and physician and became a professor of nutrition at Harvard Medical School and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.[20] A 2018 review credits his group with developing protein-sparing therapies to limit nitrogen losses both in acute illness and in low-calorie diets for obesity.[5] Papers from the mid-1970s examined nitrogen balance and insulin requirements in obese diabetic adults and nitrogen metabolism in mildly obese subjects on the diet,[4][10] and a 1977 New England Journal of Medicine paper studied it in Prader-Willi obesity.

A 1978 JAMA article on the clinical use of the diet and, in 1985, a report of 668 outpatients treated in a multidisciplinary programme built around it, marked its spread in hospital weight-management clinics.[3][11]

In 1976 Robert Linn's book The Last Chance Diet popularised a commercial liquid-protein version, and such products became widely used.[22] Wikipedia records that 58 people in the United States died in 1978 after using very-low-calorie liquid protein diets; a 1979 report by Isner described 17 sudden cardiac deaths associated with a prolonged QT interval, and a 1978 review by Bistrian noted that the implicated products relied on hydrolysed collagen with tryptophan, lacking essential amino acids.[12][21][22] The FDA has required warnings on protein VLCD products since 1984, and in 1991 the Federal Trade Commission charged three VLCD brands with deceptive advertising.[12]

sections.h: Use in physique and looksmaxxing communities
paras: Fitness writers describe PSMF as a short-term crash diet that cuts calories to a small fraction of maintenance, with nearly all calories from lean protein such as chicken breast, lean beef or white fish, low-calorie vegetables, and supplements such as fish oil, a multivitamin, electrolytes, calcium and magnesium.[18] Lyle McDonald's book is the main source for this lifter version, in which protein targets are scaled to lean body mass and to how lean the person already is.[18] A Legion Athletics article describes training as continuing with two to three resistance sessions per week built on compound lifts plus walking, rather than heavy volume.[18]

On T Nation, members have logged PSMF blocks of about six weeks to reduce body fat before a deadline, monitoring energy levels and planning to add food if needed.[2] Others describe trying it as a personal experiment while questioning how fasting-style dieting fits with building size and strength.[1] In looks-focused discussion the draw is that facial fat loss changes jawline, cheek and under-eye definition faster than a mild deficit would.

Practitioners and writers generally describe it as best suited to people carrying more body fat; Legion Athletics says muscle loss is more likely at below roughly 15 percent body fat for men or 25 percent for women, and describes it as unsuitable for people with a history of eating disorders, binge eating or repeated crash dieting.[18]

A 1990 American Family Physician review calls it a safe and effective method for losing a large amount of weight relatively quickly, to be combined with exercise, behaviour change and education, for generally healthy people with at least 40 lb to lose.[6] A 2014 Cleveland Clinic review examines its benefits for weight loss, glycemic control, insulin resistance and cardiovascular risk factors in type 2 diabetes.[13]

Across very-low-calorie diets generally, supervised programmes have produced about 4 kg more weight loss than behavioural programmes at one year, and the first one to two weeks of loss is largely water and glycogen.[12] A 1982 review noted that rapid weight loss from fasting and PSMF tends to be followed by gradual regain in long-term follow-ups.[7]

sections.h: Protein, lean mass and rate of loss: sports nutrition research
paras: A 2014 review of natural bodybuilding contest preparation, published in the Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition, recommends weight loss of about 0.5 to 1 percent of body weight per week to retain muscle, and protein of 2.3 to 3.1 g per kg of lean mass per day during a calorie deficit, with leaner competitors likely needing more.[19] It cites studies in which lean athletes on higher protein lost less lean mass than those on lower protein and notes that the leanest bodybuilders in one study lost lean mass even on high protein.[19]

This sports-nutrition literature addresses moderate deficits over weeks to months, not the much steeper deficit of a PSMF; the review advises caution about very aggressive deficits and about very-low-carbohydrate diets in contest preparation.[19] Proponents of PSMF respond that its short duration and high protein are what distinguish it from long crash diets.[18]

A study of seven obese women found resting metabolic rate fell 22 percent when the modified fast began and stayed depressed during weight maintenance.[8] Very-low-calorie diets are associated with loss of lean mass, gallstones, constipation and, if unmonitored, electrolyte disturbances that can affect heart rhythm.[12]

Clinical protocols include medical supervision, candidate selection, vitamin and mineral supplementation and sometimes an ECG before starting.[6][7][21] Fitness sources describe fatigue and hunger as common and note that rebound weight gain often follows crash diets.[18]

Controlled trials include a 1985 comparison of PSMF with a protein-formula liquid diet,[15] a 1987 controlled study of appetite and symptoms on the diet,[16] and a 2023 open-label randomised trial of a PSMF formula given by nasogastric tube versus orally in adults with a BMI above 34.9.[14] A 2023 report examined preoperative PSMF before bariatric surgery.[17] These studies were carried out in people with obesity rather than in lean physique-focused dieters, and none tested the lifter-oriented version.

timeline.event: Blackburn and colleagues describe protein-sparing modified fasting for obesity.[21]
Nitrogen metabolism study in obese diabetic adults on PSMF published in Diabetes;[4] The Last Chance Diet popularises liquid protein.[22]
Studies of PSMF in mildly obese subjects and in Prader-Willi obesity published.[10]
JAMA publishes 'Clinical use of a protein-sparing modified fast';[3] 58 US deaths among liquid protein dieters are recorded.[12]
Isner reports 17 sudden cardiac deaths among liquid protein dieters.[22]
FDA begins requiring warnings on protein VLCD products under 400 kcal a day.[12]
Results from 668 outpatients treated with a PSMF-based programme reported.[11]
American Family Physician review of the approach.[6]
Lyle McDonald's The Rapid Fat Loss Handbook adapts PSMF for bodybuilders.[18]
Cleveland Clinic review for type 2 diabetes;[13] natural bodybuilding contest-prep review recommends moderate rates of loss.[19]
Randomised trial of PSMF by nasogastric tube published.[14]

lore.intro: On T Nation and in physique writing, PSMF appears as a short cutting tool, a personal experiment and a contested method for people who already train hard.[1][2][18]

claims.claim: PSMF strips fat fast while the protein keeps muscle
claims.believers: Log authors run multi-week blocks to get lean quickly, and Legion Athletics describes less muscle loss than other crash diets when protein and training are adequate.[2][18]
claims.experts: Clinical reviews report rapid weight loss with preserved protein balance compared with total fasting, but also lean-mass concerns with very-low-calorie diets.[4][12]

claims.claim: A short PSMF lets you get lean without a long diet
claims.believers: Fitness writers say a few days to two weeks shortens time spent dieting before a return to maintenance.[18]
claims.experts: A 1982 review found regain commonly follows rapid weight loss; sports-nutrition reviewers recommend slower rates of loss of 0.5-1 percent of body weight per week for muscle retention.[7][19]

claims.claim: Fasting-style dieting does not suit building strength and size
claims.believers: One T Nation member says he is unsold on fasting-style PSMF for being jacked and strong.[1]
claims.experts: Resting metabolic rate has been reported to fall during the modified fast.[8]

claims.claim: Very lean people lose more muscle on it
claims.believers: Legion Athletics says muscle loss is more likely below about 15% body fat in men.[18]
claims.experts: The contest-prep review notes the leanest bodybuilders face greater lean-mass loss in a deficit.[19]

claims.claim: Modern PSMF is safe because it uses complete protein
claims.believers: Descriptions of the supervised diet stress complete protein, supplements and monitoring, unlike 1970s liquid collagen products.[21][22]
claims.experts: The deaths linked to 1970s liquid protein diets involved collagen-based products; guidance still limits VLCDs to supervised settings.[12][22]
